title: Being, Doing, Having: Why 50 Years of Senior Craft Lives in Context, Not Code
why_read: A dense, jargon-heavy philosophical essay about senior engineering craft and AI coding that leans heavily on self-invented terminology and self-promotional theory links.
analysis: This article tries to frame why experienced engineers outperform AI code generation using borrowed self-help language like 'being, doing, having', paired with invented terms such as 'Synthetic Scars' and numbered theorems linked to the author's own website. The heavy use of unexplained jargon and external registries makes it hard to extract concrete, verifiable technical claims from the excerpt. It reads more like promotional content for a personal framework than a rigorous technical argument about software engineering or AI limitations. There is little indication of genuinely new technical insight for engineers evaluating AI coding tools.
